payload.unusable_reason: No compensation amount is decided or stated: a three-judge bench answered a referred question of law (whether the insurer may plead negligence in a Section 163A claim) and adjourned the appeal for disposal on merits later, releasing half the deposited compensation meanwhile.

precedent.holding: In a claim for structured-formula compensation under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the insurer cannot raise any defence of negligence on the part of the victim. A Section 163A award is final and needs no proof of negligence. This answers a reference, taking the opposite view to the earlier two-judge ruling in Sinitha.

extraction.title_anon: Accident claimant, Delhi, Section 163A no-fault claim (insurer's negligence defence)
extraction.family_summary: A road accident claim for no-fault compensation under Section 163A was filed in Delhi, and the Delhi High Court decided the appeal in 2011; the judgment does not state either amount. The insurer appealed to the Supreme Court, which in 2017 held that an insurer cannot plead the victim's negligence in a Section 163A claim. The appeal itself was left to be heard later, and half the compensation held in deposit was released to the claimant.
what_mattered: Section 163A compensation is a final award on a fixed formula made without proof of fault, so the insurer cannot defend it by blaming the victim.
No amount was decided here: the appeal was adjourned to await a larger bench ruling on Section 170, with half the deposited compensation released meanwhile.
